<?php

namespace Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance;

use Drupal\Core\Config\ConfigFactoryInterface;

/**
 * Decides which routing mode is in force for this environment.
 *
 * One question, asked in one place: may the customer-route entry provider reach
 * the live Google adapter, or must it serve a deterministic recorded figure that
 * costs nothing? A ~40,000-request incident came from local development and
 * automated verification billing the live provider, so the safe answer in DDEV
 * is not a preference an operator can forget to set — it is read from the
 * environment itself.
 *
 * Two signals, in order:
 *
 * - The DDEV signal. `IS_DDEV_PROJECT=true` is present in every DDEV web
 *   container and nowhere else, and it is the same signal settings.php already
 *   trusts. When it is set, the mode is development_fixed unconditionally, so no
 *   configuration value and no stray API key can talk local development into
 *   dialling out.
 * - Otherwise configuration. `custom_webform_handlers.settings:routing_mode`
 *   selects the mode on a server that is not DDEV, defaulting to live_cached.
 *   Production can still be pinned to development_fixed through a settings.php
 *   config override without editing exported configuration.
 *
 * The environment flag is injectable so a non-billing probe can force either
 * mode with a literal — `new RoutingModeResolver($configFactory, 'false')` asks
 * the live branch even inside DDEV — without a real key and without a network.
 * Nothing here reads or stores a credential.
 */
final class RoutingModeResolver {

  /**
   * Deterministic, no-HTTP recorded routes. The mode DDEV always resolves to.
   */
  public const MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED = 'development_fixed';

  /**
   * Cache-first live Google routing. The production default.
   */
  public const MODE_LIVE_CACHED = 'live_cached';

  /**
   * The resolved DDEV signal: 'true' inside a DDEV container, '' otherwise.
   */
  private readonly string $environmentFlag;

  /**
   * Constructs the routing mode resolver.
   *
   * @param \Drupal\Core\Config\ConfigFactoryInterface $configFactory
   *   Reads the routing_mode setting when the environment does not force a mode.
   * @param string|null $environmentFlag
   *   The DDEV signal, for tests and probes. NULL — the service default — reads
   *   getenv('IS_DDEV_PROJECT') at construction. A literal ('true' / 'false')
   *   forces the branch without touching the environment, so a probe can prove
   *   either mode without a key or a request.
   */
  public function __construct(
    private readonly ConfigFactoryInterface $configFactory,
    ?string $environmentFlag = NULL,
  ) {
    $this->environmentFlag = $environmentFlag ?? (getenv('IS_DDEV_PROJECT') ?: '');
  }

  /**
   * Returns the routing mode in force, one of this class's MODE_* constants.
   */
  public function effectiveMode(): string {
    if ($this->environmentFlag === 'true') {
      return self::MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED;
    }

    $configured = (string) $this->configFactory
      ->get('custom_webform_handlers.settings')
      ->get('routing_mode');

    return $configured === self::MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED
      ? self::MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED
      : self::MODE_LIVE_CACHED;
  }

  /**
   * Returns whether no outbound routing request may be made.
   *
   * The single predicate the entry facade and the live adapter's fail-closed
   * guard both read: TRUE means serve a recorded figure and refuse the network.
   */
  public function isDevelopmentFixed(): bool {
    return $this->effectiveMode() === self::MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED;
  }

}

<?php

namespace Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance;

use Drupal\Component\Datetime\TimeInterface;

/**
 * Serves deterministic recorded routes for local development, without HTTP.
 *
 * The development half of the routing contract. It implements the same
 * DistanceProviderInterface the live Google adapter does, returns a valid
 * DistanceResult for any usable From/To pair, and never opens a socket — so a
 * developer can price a quote, save a submission, start a checkout and look up
 * dispatch slots with the network unplugged and no provider ever billed.
 *
 * It answers in two ways, in order:
 *
 * - An exact recorded fixture, when the normalized address pair's fingerprint
 *   matches one that has been pinned in FIXTURES. This is where a real
 *   cached/recorded route fact is reused — a figure actually observed and
 *   written down by an operator, keyed exactly as the live cache keys it, so a
 *   fixture reproduces a known journey to the metre. It ships empty on purpose:
 *   a fixture is added deliberately, not scraped, and the module must work
 *   before any exist.
 * - Otherwise one documented fixed fallback. Every unpinned pair resolves to the
 *   same local NYC-metro figure, which is the point — it is deterministic, it
 *   exercises courier excess-distance pricing and slot travel time, and it does
 *   not depend on any historic record existing.
 *
 * The input contract mirrors the live adapter: an empty endpoint, or two
 * endpoints that are the same address, is unusable everywhere and is refused
 * with the same classified terminal failure rather than being priced as a
 * zero-length drive.
 *
 * The result names itself development_fixed and carries data_version
 * ddev-fixed-v1, so nothing downstream can mistake a development figure for a
 * live one — the quote endpoint's client-echo gate, which trusts only
 * 'google_routes', rejects it and recomputes server-side, which here is free.
 */
final class FixedDevelopmentRouteProvider implements DistanceProviderInterface {

  /**
   * The provider identifier this provider stamps on every result.
   */
  public const PROVIDER_ID = 'development_fixed';

  /**
   * The recorded-fixture dataset version, carried in result metadata.
   */
  public const DATA_VERSION = 'ddev-fixed-v1';

  /**
   * The documented fallback distance, in meters. 19312 m is 12.0 statute miles.
   *
   * Chosen to sit above the courier included-mileage threshold (5 mi) so excess
   * distance is exercised, and well below the commercial (50 mi) and
   * long-distance tiers, so a local form test reads as a local move.
   */
  private const FALLBACK_DISTANCE_METERS = 19312;

  /**
   * The documented fallback duration, in seconds. 1680 s is 28 minutes.
   */
  private const FALLBACK_DURATION_SECONDS = 1680;

  /**
   * Exact recorded routes, keyed by DistanceResult::pairFingerprint().
   *
   * Each key is the sha256 of the two normalized, lowercased endpoints joined by
   * a NUL, and each value is [distanceMeters, durationSeconds] observed for that
   * ordered pair. Add an entry to reproduce a known journey exactly; leave it
   * empty and every pair uses the documented fallback.
   *
   * @var array<string, array{0: int, 1: int}>
   */
  private const FIXTURES = [];

  /**
   * Constructs the fixed development route provider.
   *
   * @param \Drupal\Component\Datetime\TimeInterface|null $time
   *   Supplies the calculation timestamp. NULL falls back to time(), so direct
   *   construction in a probe needs no container.
   */
  public function __construct(
    private readonly ?TimeInterface $time = NULL,
  ) {}

  /**
   * {@inheritdoc}
   */
  public function calculate(string $origin, string $destination): DistanceResult {
    $origin = DistanceResult::normalizeAddressText($origin);
    $destination = DistanceResult::normalizeAddressText($destination);
    if ($origin === ''
      || $destination === ''
      || mb_strtolower($origin, 'UTF-8') === mb_strtolower($destination, 'UTF-8')) {
      throw DistanceProviderException::classified(DistanceProviderException::ADDRESS_UNUSABLE);
    }

    $fingerprint = DistanceResult::pairFingerprint($origin, $destination);
    [$meters, $seconds] = self::FIXTURES[$fingerprint]
      ?? [self::FALLBACK_DISTANCE_METERS, self::FALLBACK_DURATION_SECONDS];

    $now = $this->time?->getCurrentTime() ?? time();

    return new DistanceResult(
      $meters,
      $seconds,
      self::PROVIDER_ID,
      $now,
      NULL,
      FALSE,
      ['data_version' => self::DATA_VERSION],
    );
  }

}

<?php

namespace Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance;

/**
 * The one customer-route entry point every quote and booking seam calls.
 *
 * Before this facade, three seams — the quote preview controller, the
 * AddressDistanceHandler pre-save, and the dispatch checkout starter — each
 * injected the live Google adapter directly and called it whenever a server key
 * was present, with nothing between them and Guzzle. That is what let local
 * development bill the live provider. Now all three inject this, and the choice
 * of provider is made once, here, from the routing mode.
 *
 * It implements DistanceProviderInterface itself, so it is a drop-in replacement
 * at every seam and adds no method a caller has to learn. It owns no cache, no
 * budget and no provider chain: development_fixed delegates to the deterministic
 * recorded provider, live_cached delegates to the unchanged Google adapter,
 * whose own cache-first behaviour and one-request-per-committed-pair controls
 * are preserved exactly. There is one authority for each mode and this picks
 * between them; it does not duplicate either.
 */
final class RoutingModeEntryProvider implements DistanceProviderInterface {

  /**
   * Constructs the customer-route entry facade.
   *
   * @param \Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance\RoutingModeResolver $resolver
   *   Decides which provider answers.
   * @param \Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance\DistanceProviderInterface $liveProvider
   *   The live, cache-first provider used in live_cached mode.
   * @param \Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance\DistanceProviderInterface $developmentProvider
   *   The deterministic no-HTTP provider used in development_fixed mode.
   */
  public function __construct(
    private readonly RoutingModeResolver $resolver,
    private readonly DistanceProviderInterface $liveProvider,
    private readonly DistanceProviderInterface $developmentProvider,
  ) {}

  /**
   * {@inheritdoc}
   */
  public function calculate(string $origin, string $destination): DistanceResult {
    $provider = $this->resolver->isDevelopmentFixed()
      ? $this->developmentProvider
      : $this->liveProvider;

    return $provider->calculate($origin, $destination);
  }

}

 *   config override without editing exported configuration.
 *
 * The environment flag is injectable so a non-billing probe can force either
 * mode with a literal — `new RoutingModeResolver($configFactory, 'false')` asks
 * the live branch even inside DDEV — without a real key and without a network.
 * Nothing here reads or stores a credential.
 */
final class RoutingModeResolver {

  /**
   * Deterministic, no-HTTP recorded routes. The mode DDEV always resolves to.
   */
  public const MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED = 'development_fixed';

  /**
   * Cache-first live Google routing. The production default.
   */
  public const MODE_LIVE_CACHED = 'live_cached';

  /**
   * The resolved DDEV signal: 'true' inside a DDEV container, '' otherwise.
   */
  private readonly string $environmentFlag;

  /**
   * Constructs the routing mode resolver.
   *
   * @param \Drupal\Core\Config\ConfigFactoryInterface $configFactory
   *   Reads the routing_mode setting when the environment does not force a mode.
   * @param string|null $environmentFlag
   *   The DDEV signal, for tests and probes. NULL — the service default — reads
   *   getenv('IS_DDEV_PROJECT') at construction. A literal ('true' / 'false')
   *   forces the branch without touching the environment, so a probe can prove
   *   either mode without a key or a request.
   */
  public function __construct(
    private readonly ConfigFactoryInterface $configFactory,
    ?string $environmentFlag = NULL,
  ) {
    $this->environmentFlag = $environmentFlag ?? (getenv('IS_DDEV_PROJECT') ?: '');
  }

  /**
   * Returns the routing mode in force, one of this class's MODE_* constants.
   */
  public function effectiveMode(): string {
    if ($this->environmentFlag === 'true') {
      return self::MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED;
    }

    $configured = (string) $this->configFactory
      ->get('custom_webform_handlers.settings')
      ->get('routing_mode');

    return $configured === self::MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED
      ? self::MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED
      : self::MODE_LIVE_CACHED;
  }

  /**
   * Returns whether no outbound routing request may be made.
   *
   * The single predicate the entry facade and the live adapter's fail-closed
   * guard both read: TRUE means serve a recorded figure and refuse the network.
   */
  public function isDevelopmentFixed(): bool {
    return $this->effectiveMode() === self::MODE_DEVELOPMENT_FIXED;
  }

}

<?php

namespace Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance;

use Drupal\Component\Datetime\TimeInterface;

/**
 * Serves deterministic recorded routes for local development, without HTTP.
 *
 * The development half of the routing contract. It implements the same
 * DistanceProviderInterface the live Google adapter does, returns a valid
 * DistanceResult for any usable From/To pair, and never opens a socket — so a
 * developer can price a quote, save a submission, start a checkout and look up
 * dispatch slots with the network unplugged and no provider ever billed.
 *
 * It answers in two ways, in order:
 *
 * - An exact recorded fixture, when the normalized address pair's fingerprint
 *   matches one that has been pinned in FIXTURES. This is where a real
 *   cached/recorded route fact is reused — a figure actually observed and
 *   written down by an operator, keyed exactly as the live cache keys it, so a
 *   fixture reproduces a known journey to the metre. It ships empty on purpose:
 *   a fixture is added deliberately, not scraped, and the module must work
 *   before any exist.
 * - Otherwise one documented fixed fallback. Every unpinned pair resolves to the
 *   same local NYC-metro figure, which is the point — it is deterministic, it
 *   exercises courier excess-distance pricing and slot travel time, and it does
 *   not depend on any historic record existing.
 *
 * The input contract mirrors the live adapter: an empty endpoint, or two
 * endpoints that are the same address, is unusable everywhere and is refused
 * with the same classified terminal failure rather than being priced as a
 * zero-length drive.
 *
 * The result names itself development_fixed and carries data_version
 * ddev-fixed-v1, so nothing downstream can mistake a development figure for a
 * live one — the quote endpoint's client-echo gate, which trusts only
 * 'google_routes', rejects it and recomputes server-side, which here is free.
 */
final class FixedDevelopmentRouteProvider implements DistanceProviderInterface {

  /**
   * The provider identifier this provider stamps on every result.
   */
  public const PROVIDER_ID = 'development_fixed';

  /**
   * The recorded-fixture dataset version, carried in result metadata.
   */
  public const DATA_VERSION = 'ddev-fixed-v1';

  /**
   * The documented fallback distance, in meters. 19312 m is 12.0 statute miles.
   *
   * Chosen to sit above the courier included-mileage threshold (5 mi) so excess
   * distance is exercised, and well below the commercial (50 mi) and
   * long-distance tiers, so a local form test reads as a local move.
   */
  private const FALLBACK_DISTANCE_METERS = 19312;

  /**
   * The documented fallback duration, in seconds. 1680 s is 28 minutes.
   */
  private const FALLBACK_DURATION_SECONDS = 1680;

  /**
   * Exact recorded routes, keyed by DistanceResult::pairFingerprint().
   *
   * Each key is the sha256 of the two normalized, lowercased endpoints joined by
   * a NUL, and each value is [distanceMeters, durationSeconds] observed for that
   * ordered pair. Add an entry to reproduce a known journey exactly; leave it
   * empty and every pair uses the documented fallback.
   *
   * @var array<string, array{0: int, 1: int}>
   */
  private const FIXTURES = [];

  /**
   * Constructs the fixed development route provider.
   *
   * @param \Drupal\Component\Datetime\TimeInterface|null $time
   *   Supplies the calculation timestamp. NULL falls back to time(), so direct
   *   construction in a probe needs no container.
   */
  public function __construct(
    private readonly ?TimeInterface $time = NULL,
  ) {}

  /**
   * {@inheritdoc}
   */
  public function calculate(string $origin, string $destination): DistanceResult {
    $origin = DistanceResult::normalizeAddressText($origin);
    $destination = DistanceResult::normalizeAddressText($destination);
    if ($origin === ''
      || $destination === ''
      || mb_strtolower($origin, 'UTF-8') === mb_strtolower($destination, 'UTF-8')) {
      throw DistanceProviderException::classified(DistanceProviderException::ADDRESS_UNUSABLE);
    }

    $fingerprint = DistanceResult::pairFingerprint($origin, $destination);
    [$meters, $seconds] = self::FIXTURES[$fingerprint]
      ?? [self::FALLBACK_DISTANCE_METERS, self::FALLBACK_DURATION_SECONDS];

    $now = $this->time?->getCurrentTime() ?? time();

    return new DistanceResult(
      $meters,
      $seconds,
      self::PROVIDER_ID,
      $now,
      NULL,
      FALSE,
      ['data_version' => self::DATA_VERSION],
    );
  }

}

<?php

namespace Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance;

/**
 * The one customer-route entry point every quote and booking seam calls.
 *
 * Before this facade, three seams — the quote preview controller, the
 * AddressDistanceHandler pre-save, and the dispatch checkout starter — each
 * injected the live Google adapter directly and called it whenever a server key
 * was present, with nothing between them and Guzzle. That is what let local
 * development bill the live provider. Now all three inject this, and the choice
 * of provider is made once, here, from the routing mode.
 *
 * It implements DistanceProviderInterface itself, so it is a drop-in replacement
 * at every seam and adds no method a caller has to learn. It owns no cache, no
 * budget and no provider chain: development_fixed delegates to the deterministic
 * recorded provider, live_cached delegates to the unchanged Google adapter,
 * whose own cache-first behaviour and one-request-per-committed-pair controls
 * are preserved exactly. There is one authority for each mode and this picks
 * between them; it does not duplicate either.
 */
final class RoutingModeEntryProvider implements DistanceProviderInterface {

  /**
   * Constructs the customer-route entry facade.
   *
   * @param \Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance\RoutingModeResolver $resolver
   *   Decides which provider answers.
   * @param \Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance\DistanceProviderInterface $liveProvider
   *   The live, cache-first provider used in live_cached mode.
   * @param \Drupal\custom_webform_handlers\Distance\DistanceProviderInterface $developmentProvider
   *   The deterministic no-HTTP provider used in development_fixed mode.
   */
  public function __construct(
    private readonly RoutingModeResolver $resolver,
    private readonly DistanceProviderInterface $liveProvider,
    private readonly DistanceProviderInterface $developmentProvider,
  ) {}

  /**
   * {@inheritdoc}
   */
  public function calculate(string $origin, string $destination): DistanceResult {
    $provider = $this->resolver->isDevelopmentFixed()
      ? $this->developmentProvider
      : $this->liveProvider;

    return $provider->calculate($origin, $destination);
  }

}
